title: Design System: TimTech Solutions – Tim D. Walter

display.purpose: The single h1 per page (hero statement, PageIntro titles). 68px desktop, 52px from sm, 42px mobile.

headline.purpose: Section headings in the margin column. 40px desktop, 32px mobile.

title.purpose: Row and block titles in ruled rows and text blocks; project titles 24px.

lead.purpose: Intro paragraph under a page title and the About story. 20px desktop, 18px mobile, max 52ch.

body-sm.purpose: Row bodies, summaries, actions, links, nav.

label.purpose: Real metadata only: roles, dates, categories, stack. Sentence case, no tracking.

motion.name: rise
motion.value: rise 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; from opacity 0, translateY(10px)
motion.purpose: The only load animation: staggered page opening (PageIntro / hero).

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: Delay between children; the margin column continues the sequence at 240ms / 320ms.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover and active colour changes on links, actions and nav.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .stagger > * { animation: none } html { scroll-behavior: auto } }
motion.purpose: Content simply appears; colour transitions on controls stay.

narrative.overview:
Every page reads like a page from a technical journal or a well-kept documentation site: a narrow margin column on the left carries headings, facts and metadata; a wide main column on the right carries the text. Nothing floats, nothing is boxed. Order comes from a 12-column grid, 1px hairline rules between rows and a strong size jump between a serif display face and a quiet sans body. The page is warm off-white paper with near-black ink; colour is almost absent, so the one accent carries meaning wherever it appears.

The system is a deliberate replacement for an earlier card-based look. It refuses the SaaS landing page: no centred hero, no badges or pills over the headline, no card grids, no gradients, glows or shadows, no decorative icons. Variation between sections comes from the form of the content (two-column text blocks, ruled rows, an index of dates and titles), never from decoration.

Density is generous: sections breathe on a 48/96px rhythm, body text stays under ~52ch, and the desktop grid deliberately leaves one column empty as air between margin and content.
keyCharacteristics: Asymmetric 12-column grid: margin column 1–3, column 4 empty, main column 5–12.
1px hairline rules instead of boxes; lists of things are ruled rows.
Fraunces display at regular weight against IBM Plex Sans body; IBM Plex Mono only for real metadata.
Paper, ink, grey and exactly one accent (darkened logo cyan).
Square corners, no shadows, one staggered load animation.
One dark block per page: the closing contact section.

rules.name: The Closed Palette Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's colour palette is replaced, not extended: paper, ink, muted, rule, accent, accent-dark and logo are the only colours that exist. Opacity variants of these (paper at 70%, accent at 40% for link underlines) are the only derivations.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent marks something actionable or current – a link, the active page, a status – and appears at most once as a highlight per section. It is never a background panel, never decoration.

rules.name: The 3x Jump Rule
rules.body: The page headline is at least three times body size on desktop (68px over 20px lead). Recorded exception: on mobile it is 42px over 18px, because German compounds would overflow at a larger size.

rules.name: The Honest Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for real metadata – years, roles, categories, stack – always in sentence case without letter-spacing. Never tracked uppercase labels, never a kicker above a heading; classification lives in the margin column.

rules.name: The Regular Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings are Fraunces at weight 400 with slight negative tracking and balanced wrapping; emphasis comes from size, not boldness. Medium (500) is used only for action labels, the name and the current language code.

rules.name: The Empty Column Rule
rules.body: Column 4 is never filled on desktop. It is the air that keeps the headline from touching the portrait and gives the page its asymmetry.

rules.name: The Token Spacing Rule
rules.body: Spacing uses only the named scale (4 / 8 / 16 / 24 / 48 / 96px as xs–2xl). Numeric Tailwind steps are legacy and do not belong in redesigned work.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Raised Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line, never a shadow or a box. A heavier 1px ink rule (instead of stone) marks a set of equal-weight principles; that is the only rule-weight variation.

dos: Do build new sections from the existing blocks: DocSection, PageIntro, RuledRows, ProjectRows, ArticleRows, MainColumn, TextLink and the contact block.
Do keep headings and classification in the margin column (1–3) and content in the main column (5–12), leaving column 4 empty on desktop.
Do separate items with 1px stone rules and keep lists as ruled rows.
Do use only paper, ink, muted, rule, accent, accent-dark and logo, and only the 4 / 8 / 16 / 24 / 48 / 96px spacing names.
Do keep the h1 at least 3× body size on desktop; the mobile 42/18px ratio is the one recorded exception.
Do cap running text at 52ch and bind spaced dashes to the preceding word so no line starts with a dash.
Do keep WCAG AA contrast, the visible 2px accent focus outline, unbroken heading levels and no functional text below 11px.
Do keep the existing generated project images (SH-Beach, LH-Leap, Digital Aristoteles, Darth Vader, Not Found) – the owner's explicit exception – shown whole in square frames.
donts: Don't use gradients (especially purple/blue/indigo), gradient text, aurora or glow backgrounds.
Don't use drop shadows, glassmorphism or blur.
Don't build identical three-column card grids, bento grids, icon-plus-heading tiles, or skill badges with logos.
Don't use rounded pill buttons or pill badges above the headline ("New", "Available for work").
Don't set kickers or eyebrows above headings, tracked uppercase labels, numbering on non-sequences, or arrows on links.
Don't use Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Space Grotesk or a system font stack, and don't load fonts from a CDN.
Don't attach decorative icons to headings; icons are for function only (the mobile menu toggle).
Don't scatter micro-animations, scroll reveals or hover scale; the staggered page opening is the only load animation.
Don't use the light logo cyan for text or highlights on paper.
Don't add new generated or stock images, invented figures, placeholder quotes or testimonials.
Don't centre standard blocks in a Hero → Features → Testimonials → CTA sequence.
